head: claude/ml-backlog-drain-manifest-contract
title: ml-backlog drain: refute the manifest-side fix, ship the commit-time guard that is decidable
body:
## What this is

Backlog drain #2. Scope was **exactly one file — `docs/claude/ml-review-backlog.json`** — and no other backlog file, and not `OPEN-ITEMS.json`, was touched. Sibling drains hold those.

**Burn-down: 22 unresolved → 22 unresolved. I closed nothing.** The honest reason is below, and I think it is the most useful thing in this PR: the high-severity row's prescribed fix is aimed at the wrong side of the contract, and I can show that rather than assert it.

---

## Denominator

At the sha I branched from (`de61ead`):

| | count |
|---|---|
| rows in file | 106 |
| `resolved` | 84 |
| **unresolved** | **22** |
| — of which `open` | 3 (1 high, 2 medium) |
| — of which `kept_open` | 19 |
| — snoozed past 2026-09-02 | 2 (`MB-20260613-002` → 11-01, `MB-20260627-003` → 09-30), so **20 due** |

**Examined:** all 22 (title / status / criteria). **Examined with a measurement:** 4.
**CLOSED 0 · REFUSED 3 · annotated-not-refused 1 · FILED 0.**

Reconciled against this PR's head: 106 rows, 84 `resolved`, 22 unresolved (3 `open` + 19 `kept_open`) — **identical**. No status changed. `git diff --numstat` on the backlog file is **30 insertions / 2 deletions** (not the ~21k a naive read-append-write produces); the file's serialisation was detected with `backlog_append.detect_format` and re-asserted byte-exact after writing.

---

## Was there a real class? YES — and it is not the class the row describes

The two newest `open` rows and `MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD` are one root cause. But the high-severity row prescribes the wrong remedy for it, and that is the finding.

### The measurement that refutes the prescribed fix

`MB-20260829-MANIFESTS-DECLARE-COLUMNS-…-NOTHING-CHECKS-AT-COMMIT` asks for a commit-time check that a manifest's declared `feature_columns` "are producible by its declared dataset family", and names **10 columns across 3 manifests** as what it would catch.

I resolved every manifest's `dataset.family` to its builder class via `ml/datasets/registry.py::FAMILY_REGISTRY` and diffed declared `feature_columns` + `target_column` against that builder's `schema` ClassVar.

- **Population: all 76 manifests** under `ml/configs/*.yaml` (79 dir entries = 76 `.yaml` + 2 `.yaml.disabled` + 1 `retired/` dir).
- **Result: 0 offenders.**
- **Positive control** (this is why the zero means anything): injecting `__NOT_A_REAL_COLUMN__` into the same probe **is** flagged. The probe finds a positive before I trust its negative.
- **All 10 of the row's cause-A columns are in their builder's schema**: `log_return_lag_1` / `log_return_lag_2` / `hour_of_day` / `dayofweek` (market_features), the four yang-zhang estimators (setup_candidates), `killzone` / `bias` (setup_labels).

**The manifest is not the wrong side of that contract in a single one of those cases.** A guard built to the row's stated criteria would merge green and catch none of the 8 instances that motivated it.

### The real mechanism — read off the field

The row's own `next_action` says to resolve the puzzling instance first. It resolves cleanly:

`btc-regime-15m-lgbm-base-vt003-pcv-v1`'s feature list is **identical** to its sibling `btc-regime-15m-lgbm-base-pcv-v003`. The only difference is `dataset.version` **v001 vs v003**.

- `ml/datasets/builder.py:45` — a shard resolves to `<root>/<family>/<symbol_scope>/<timeframe>/<version>/`, where `version` is a hand-chosen label.
- `ml/datasets/families/market_features.py:412-414` — in the builder's own words, `builder_version` "is metadata-only (**it does not gate dataset path resolution**)".
- `ml/datasets/builder.py:134` — a rebuild into an existing version dir **raises**.

So a shard materialised under an older builder keeps its narrower schema permanently, and a manifest pinning that version silently reads the stale shard. The four "absent" columns were added by market_features builder **v2** (its own changelog comment, line 375); the builder is now at **v12**.

### Live corroboration — one freeze event, not four typos

Off `/api/bot/ml/registry` (a trainer mirror, `mirror_age_seconds` **21.5** at read, 96 rows, HTTP 200 — sibling paths `/api/bot/ml/models` and `/api/bot/models` both 404, so the 200 is a real route and not a catch-all):

Of the 76 in-repo manifests, **73** carry a registry row and 3 have none. Exactly **4** of the 73 have a `latest_run` past the trainer's 7-day threshold — and **all four last trained on the same day, 2026-07-26**:

| manifest | dataset_ref | last run | age |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setup-quality-lgbm-v2` | setup_labels/all/all/**v002** | 2026-07-26T06:01:49Z | 37.8d |
| `setup-candidates-metalabel-xsym-yz-v1` | setup_candidates/all/all/**v001** | 2026-07-26T06:01:47Z | 37.8d |
| `btc-regime-15m-lgbm-base-vt003-pcv-v1` | market_features/BTCUSDT/15m/**v001** | 2026-07-26T05:29:33Z | 37.8d |
| `prop-mission-policy-baseline-v0` | account_context/all/all/**v001** | 2026-07-26T05:20:08Z | 37.8d |

Every one pins a low version string while its builder has advanced. `MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD` was opened at 08:45Z **that same morning** — the four runs are 05:20–06:01Z. That row diagnosed this exact mechanism for one manifest in July; it is a class of four.

---

## What shipped: `scripts/ci/check_manifest_scope_constants.py`

The commit-time half — restricted to what is genuinely decidable **without** a dataset:

- **C1 — structurally constant feature.** A declared feature the manifest's own `dataset:` scope pins to one value: `hour_of_day` on a bar ≥ 1d, `dayofweek` on ≥ 1w, `symbol` when `symbol_scope` names one symbol, `timeframe` when it is not `all`. **This is the real `mes-regime-1d-lgbm-v2` defect** — 34.0 days untrained under a green rc=0 cycle.
- **C2 — column no builder emits.** Kept as a regression guard and **honestly labelled in its own docstring as never having fired on this repo's history**, with the 0/76 measurement written down so a future green run cannot be read as covering the class.
- **C3 — categorical not in `feature_columns`.** `ml/trainers/lightgbm_multiclass.py:119-123` **raises** on this at train time — a hard failure, strictly worse than the silent skip. C3 exists because it is precisely the trap a naive C1 fix falls into: `hour_of_day` was in *both* lists on the mes-1d manifest, so removing it from `feature_columns` alone would have converted a skipped manifest into a crashing one.

### The failure path is exercised, not assumed

`guard_selftests.py::selftest_manifest_scope_constants`, wired into `run_guards.py` and verified by `check_selftest_wiring.py` (12/12 self-tests resolve to a covering path).

Watched it actually fail, planting the **real historical defect**:

```
################ PLANT C1 — hour_of_day on a 1d bar (the real mes-regime-1d manifest)
manifest-scope-constants: 77 manifest(s) ...; 65 declare feature_columns ...
::error::a manifest declares something that cannot work. ...
  - [scope_constant] _demo-c1-mes-1d: hour_of_day — dataset.timeframe 1d spans >= the
    period of hour_of_day, so it has ONE value by construction
>>> EXIT=1

################ CONTROL — the same manifest at 15m, where the hour genuinely varies
OK — no manifest declares a feature its own dataset scope makes constant, ...
>>> EXIT=0
```

**The negative control is the one that matters.** The obvious over-broad C1 flags `hour_of_day` everywhere — and 54 of the 55 manifests declaring it are on 5m/15m/1h/all bars where the hour genuinely varies. Such a guard passes every positive test and then fails the whole fleet. It is asserted, not assumed.

---

## REFUSED (3)

**1. `MB-20260829-MANIFESTS-DECLARE-COLUMNS-…-NOTHING-CHECKS-AT-COMMIT` — high.**
Measured above. Stays open for two honest reasons: (a) the shard-side half **cannot** be checked at commit time — CI has no shards — and belongs where the shards are, comparing each shard's own `metadata.json` `schema`/`builder_version` (`ml/datasets/metadata.py` already records both) against the manifest; that is unbuilt. (b) The row also requires each of the 7 failing manifests to train again or be explicitly retired, which needs trainer evidence I could not reach. **I have proposed an amendment to its `resolution_criteria` in the row's annotation**, because as written the criterion is satisfiable by a guard that provably catches none of its own instances.

**2. `MB-20260829-MES-1D-DECLARES-A-FEATURE-THAT-CANNOT-VARY-AT-ITS-OWN-TIMEFRAME` — medium.**
**Criterion (a) IS satisfied**: `mes-regime-1d-lgbm-v2` reads `deployment_bucket SHADOW`, `runs=55`, `latest_run.at 2026-09-02T01:03:30Z` — ~28 min before my read, well after #10414 deployed. A registered run is strictly stronger than the two things the criterion excludes (a YAML parse; absence of the audit flag). **Criterion (b) is half-met**: the stale cohort **reduced 7 → 4** (measured), and `mes-regime-5m-lgbm-macro-v1` — one of the five sibling skips — now trains too (0.02d old, runs=78). But (b) also requires *"the other five enforced skips each have a NAMED cause read from `dataset_audit.jsonl` (not inferred)"*, and I could not do that read. The row says the first alone does not close it, and it is right. **One correction to its arithmetic**: the never-trained population reads as **3**, not 2 — `exit-policy-v1`, `mes-execution-quality-baseline-v0` and `setup-candidates-metalabel-paper-v1` have no registry row at all.

**3. `MB-20260822-ETH-15M-HEAD-IS-AT-CANDIDATE-NOT-SHADOW` — medium.**
I ran the row's own observable criterion against the surface it names, today. **Negative.** Zero ETH 15m heads at SHADOW/LIVE clear macro_f1 0.5840; the two at SHADOW are `eth-regime-15m-lgbm-xasset-v1` (0.48174) and `eth-regime-15m-lgbm-selfonly-v901ctrl` (0.45757). **Positive control is exact**: the same filter reproduces the row's own 2026-08-22 figures (0.4817 / 0.4576) to 4 d.p. Corroborated in the same read: `eth-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1` is OFFLINE at macro_f1 0.584044, matching both the cited 0.5840 and the operator-approved 2026-07-19 demotion. The row now turns entirely on its other branch — a proposed `-fc-pcv-v2` manifest or a written decision that ETH stays unmodelled at 15m. Both are new modelling work / a decision, not a drain action, and I did not manufacture either. Re-promoting the demoted head stays forbidden.

## Annotated, not refused (1)

`MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD` — correctly parked (the fix is a trainer-side `--overwrite` rebuild). Confirmed still stale live (OFFLINE, 37.8d, pinned `v001` against `SetupCandidatesBuilder.builder_version = v2`), and upgraded from an isolated side-stream to one of the four class members above. Its "rebuild when the track is next activated" trigger is right for this manifest but under-scoped as a remedy: the same rebuild is owed on three others, and nothing detects the next one.

---

## Caveats — what I inferred vs observed

- **The trainer was unreachable to me**, and this bounds two refusals. It has no HTTP diag API, and the `trainer-vm-diag` issue relay is closed to this session: `create issue` returns **403 `Resource not accessible by integration`** (a write-scope boundary, not a transient drop). There is a file-drop relay for PRs and for board posts, but **none for diag requests**. So `dataset_audit.jsonl` and `training_cycle.jsonl` were never read by me.
- **Everything I claim about the shard side is inferred from code, not observed on disk.** I read `builder.py`, `market_features.py` and `metadata.py`; I did **not** read a single `metadata.json` off the trainer. The stale-shard mechanism is a code-plus-live-registry inference. It is strongly corroborated (identical sibling manifests differing only in version; all four freezing the same day; each pinning a low version) but it is not the direct read, and the direct read is one `ls` on the trainer away for whoever has that access.
- **`mes-regime-1d` criterion (a)**: I read the *registered run*, not a `training_cycle.jsonl` `manifest_ok` row. I consider the former stronger; the row asked for both.
- **The guard's C2 arm currently finds nothing and I am not claiming otherwise** — said in the guard's own docstring, not just here.
- Locally, `run_guards.py --all` reports **PASS 65 · FAIL 3**. All three failures are **missing tooling in this sandbox**, not the diff: `pytest` is not installed (2 guards) and `lint-imports` exits 127 (1 guard). CI is the real verdict.

---

## FOR THE MANAGER

**No `OPEN-ITEMS.json` row is cleared by my evidence, and I want to be explicit about the near-miss** rather than let someone re-derive it:

`OI-20260829-TRAINER-IS-NOW-A-DECIDED-DEPENDENCY-AND-IS-UNMONITORED` looks adjacent — I demonstrated a live trainer surface (`/api/bot/ml/registry`, carrying `mirror_age_seconds`) that this session used successfully as trainer evidence. **It does not clear the row, and must not be read as doing so.** That row's `clears_when` wants an alarm keyed on the *capture data's* freshness, shown to fire against planted staleness. `mirror_age_seconds` is a freshness signal on the **mirror publish timer** — which is exactly the signal the row's own `detail` already rules out ("`trainer_reachability_alert` reads the PUBLISH timer's mirror mtime, which advances normally with the capture dead"). So this is a *confirmed negative*, not a lead.

**One thing that may want your routing:** the `/api/bot/ml/registry` mirror is a usable trainer-evidence surface for read-only sessions whose issue-create is 403. It is not documented in `docs/claude/diag-relay.md`, which currently tells such a session that the trainer is reachable only via the issue relay — and that relay is unavailable to a 403'd session, which is how this class of work stalls. That is a docs gap in a Tier I did not want to widen scope into unilaterally; say the word and I will file it or fix it.
